        Completed In progress Blocked Delayed/past due Not started | Stages: FD Functional Design · TD Tech Design · UT Unit Testing · FT Functional Testing · CP Code Promotion

        Sub-task boxes are consolidated into five stages. Each stage’s color comes from its current open Jira sub-task (the first one in that stage that is not Completed, Done, or Withdrawn): delayed if that sub-task’s Planned Complete Date is before today, on track if it is still open and not past due. Withdrawn is closed, the same as Completed, and is not a blocker. Expand a RICE item for the full sub-task list and associated change requests.

        How to read the P2 RICE Tracker

        Five stages: Functional Design (functional design, review, approval, FSD handoff) · Tech Design (technical analysis, technical design, review, approval, build) · Unit Testing · Functional Testing (handoff, functional testing, defect resolution) · Code Promotion (code promotion, update technical design). Dual-track labels such as Coupa IH / ERPP roll into the same stage.

        On track vs delayed: a stage that has not started stays cream. A fully completed stage uses the completed color. Once a stage has started, its color is taken only from the current open sub-task in that stage — delayed if that sub-task is past its Planned Complete Date, on track if it is still within date, brown if it is Blocked. Completed, Done, and Withdrawn are closed, so a Withdrawn step is skipped and the stage advances to the next incomplete step.

        P2 RICE at risk: the list includes every item that is not Complete, and Complete items that still have at least one open CR. Complete items with no open CR are omitted.

        Columns: RICE item, Jira status (current open sub-task / parent status), the five stages, and open CRs. The last count is linked change requests that still have an open defect — expand the row to see those CRs first.

        System of record: Jira remains authoritative. This is a read-only snapshot dated 3 November 2026.

        Defects

        Severity Opened today Total to date Open Resolved

        Opened today is defects raised on the snapshot date. Total to date is every defect in the selected filter at that severity. Non-conversion is the rest. Both shows the two sets together. Defect Type New Requirement is excluded.

        How to read the P2 Testing Execution tab / About this data

        Scope: Xray Test Execution issues in project CONAMER1001932 with Test Cycle = P2 and label not conversion. Defects are every Jira defect with Test Cycle = P2, including defects that are not linked to a test execution. The Defects filter shows non-conversion, conversion (label conversion), or both. Test execution counts stay on the non-conversion tests.

        P2 summary: Testers (unique assignees), Tests (in-scope count), and Execution rate (executed ÷ all in-scope tests). Executed includes tests completed before their due date. Left panel is Today vs To date for Pass / Fail / Pass with minor defect (Retest) / Withdrawn, then the other Jira statuses on these test executions: To Do, Executing, Blocked, and On Hold. Right panel is total defects (open and resolved), open defects by severity, and Resolved.

        Status mapping (Wave 2B): Jira Pass→Passed, Fail→Failed, Retest→Retest, Withdrawn→Withdrawn, To Do→Open, Executing→In Progress. Executed = Passed, Failed, Retest, or Withdrawn, including tests completed before their due date. Deferred defects count as Resolved.

        Overall execution: Executed ÷ all in-scope test cases. A test is executed when it is Passed, Failed, Retest, or Withdrawn, including tests completed before their due date. Not executed is Open, In Progress, Blocked, and On Hold.

        Overdue: not executed and not Withdrawn, with a due date before the snapshot date. Withdrawn test executions are left out of every overdue count. Ready to test now is overdue and Open or In Progress. Blocked / on hold is overdue and Blocked or On Hold. Due dates come from Jira’s standard Due date field.

        Key blockers: the open defects linked to the most blocked or on-hold test cases.

        Critical and High defects: open defects in the selected Defects filter with severity Critical or High (from Jira Priority, else Complexity). Past due means the Jira due date is before the snapshot date.

        Defects: Every defect with Test Cycle P2, linked to a test execution or not. Non-conversion is that set without the conversion label. Conversion is that set with the label. Defect Type New Requirement is excluded on this tab and on Data Conversion. Total is every defect in the selected filter. Open is every selected defect not Resolved (including Ready for Retest). Resolved includes Deferred / Completed / Rejected.

        Overall status: On track when executed tests, including those completed early, are at least 95% of the test cases due before the snapshot date. Tests due on the snapshot date are not included in the expected count yet. Behind plan when it is lower.

        Dates: snapshot –. Source: Jira.

        Open conversion defects by type

        Open Jira defects labeled Conversion, excluding Defect Type New Requirement, grouped by Defect Type.
        How to read this dashboard / About this data

        Conversion objects and subtasks: Jira Conversion Execution subtasks for Release 1 - P2. Withdrawn objects are excluded. The Executive Summary uses Data Conversion records only; Release 1 - P2 Prep never contributes to these metrics.

        Defects: open Jira defects labeled conversion that have fixVersion Wave 3 (including functional-team defects) or component Release 1 and Test Cycle P2 (including defects with no fix version). Defect Type New Requirement is excluded. On Hold defects remain in the open count and are labeled On Hold; they are not blockers. The table at the bottom groups those open defects by Jira Defect Type.

        Risk: any past-due conversion subtask, plus any past-due open defect of Critical or High severity. Medium, Low, and On Hold items stay on the dashboard but are not raised as Risks. Recon-related work is excluded from Risks and Blockers because it does not gate downstream activity.

        Blocker: only an item whose Jira status is exactly Blocked. The dashboard does not infer blockers, and On Hold never counts as Blocked.

        Key blocker / issue: an overdue Extract-through-Load subtask with a Jira predecessor link to downstream work. The section lists those linked items when they exist and shows a readiness note when they do not.

        % of Subtasks Complete: completed conversion subtasks ÷ all in-scope conversion subtasks. It is not an average of object statuses.

        Dates and freshness: defect Target Retest comes directly from Jira Due Date. The timestamp above records the latest Jira refresh.

        System of record: Jira remains authoritative. This is a read-only daily snapshot; records cannot be edited in the dashboard.

        Out of scope: Jira Action Items are not included. This dashboard contains only Conversion Execution subtasks and open conversion defects in the Wave 3 or Release 1 P2 scope above.
